PullRequest.Title: Send the Copilot billable owner on core's assignments request
PullRequest.Body:
sends `github_core_copilotbillableentityid` on core's assignments request, from the optional `billable_owner` field in the `copilot_internal/user` entitlements (who pays for the user's Copilot). this is the same value the Copilot Chat extension sends (#346433), so experiments that randomize by company get the same variant in core and in chat.

- `IEntitlementsData` gets the field; `ChatEntitlementService` keeps the universal key when both `universal_key` and `account_type` are non-empty strings, and stores it with the rest of the entitlement state.
- `GitHubCoreAssignmentsFilterProvider` adds the filter only when there's a value, and a change in only this value fires `onDidChangeFilters`, so assignments refetch.
- github.com only returns the field when its flag is on for the user, so there's no client flag.

tests in `chatEntitlementService.test.ts` and `assignmentFilters.test.ts`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup or sign-in initializes Copilot entitlement state and performs the initial assignments fetch
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing default-account load and TAS client initialization remain on the startup/first-treatment path. Parsing billable_owner is constant-time local work; the initial assignments request already existed and now serializes one additional optional string filter.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the persisted profile entitlement context, which may now contain billableOwnerKey.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing profile-storage read when the lazy entitlement context is instantiated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same stored entitlement object was read without the optional billable-owner field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Supplies warm entitlement state synchronously before filters are constructed; the diff only adds a small optional string to the existing object.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: POST the initial TAS assignments request through IRequestService.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial request per TAS client generation; the filter set has one additional scalar entry when available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same initial request was sent without github_core_copilotbillableentityid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing initial-fetch boundary for current assignments; the diff does not add another request or move it earlier.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build the small fixed-size filter map consumed by the TAS request serializer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One map entry added to a fixed enum-sized map per request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The fixed filter map contained three GitHub-account entries instead of four.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Constant additional payload/allocation with no scaling collection.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One account, one optional owner key, and a fixed-size filter map; cost does not scale with repositories, extensions, files, or assignment count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The TAS client owns the initial fetch. The provider constructor reads the current entitlement once; later context-key events are deduplicated against cached filter values. No collection fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm startup loads the existing persisted entitlement context, including the owner when known; cold startup has undefined until entitlement resolution. The provider's cached scalar comparison suppresses duplicate events, while the initial TAS fetch uses whichever value is currently available.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor, storage, filter-provider, and TAS initialization paths were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact request latency varies by network, but the changed CPU, storage size, and request-body size are constant and negligible; request cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: startup retains the same expensive boundaries and adds only constant-time parsing plus one scalar payload field.

Scenarios.Scenario: An entitlement refresh, account switch, sign-out, or server-side billable-owner transition updates assignment targeting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The pre-existing entitlement/default-account refresh completes first. The changed code updates one context key; GitHubCoreAssignmentsFilterProvider compares all effective values and only then requests an assignments refresh when the owner actually differs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh account entitlement data from the account service when explicitly requested.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pre-existing entitlement refresh for the user action or account event; parsing billable_owner performs no additional call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same entitlement refresh occurred but ignored billable_owner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The new owner is available only after this existing request; the diff does not introduce or increase entitlement-fetch cardinality.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the updated entitlement context to profile storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing store operation when the overall entitlement state changes; adding or changing the owner changes the object by one scalar field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same update stored the entitlement context without billableOwnerKey; owner-only changes did not exist in local state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing context update persists before context keys are propagated; no extra per-item writes are added.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh TAS assignments so experiments use the new billable entity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One effective request per actual owner transition when idle; concurrent/repeated events coalesce, with at most one trailing request if a transition occurs during an in-flight refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Owner-only changes were ignored and caused no assignments refetch; changes to existing tracking/internal filters already used the same refetch path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This boundary is intentionally introduced for owner-only changes so targeting becomes current; it is asynchronous and does not block the entitlement update itself.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Actual billable-owner transitions for one signed-in account, normally zero or a small number per session; there is no per-assignment or per-resource multiplier.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: WorkbenchAssignmentService serializes assignment refreshes behind refetchPromise. Multiple filter events during an in-flight call are collapsed into at most one trailing immediate refresh via refetchAfterFilterChange; when plan and owner change in one context update, the provider reads final state on the first event and suppresses subsequent duplicate events.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The persisted owner supplies a warm value. Equality checks suppress identical refresh responses, including repeated identical owner keys. Undefined is a meaningful absence and transitions to or from it cause a single refresh. Assignment fetches are in-flight coalesced rather than cached by owner key.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed context-key event was traced through provider equality checks to the refetchPromise/coalescing logic and request transport.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Network duration is environment-dependent, but transitions are low-cardinality and explicitly require a fresh assignment response; no unbounded retry or burst mechanism is present.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the one newly reachable network refresh is necessary for changed targeting, bounded by actual owner transitions, duplicate-suppressed, and coalesced under concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Repeated entitlement responses preserve and expose billable-owner state to context-key consumers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After an entitlement response, parseBillableOwner validates two fields, the context update compares serialized state, and unchanged state exits before persistence or context propagation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON stringify the small entitlement state for equality and tracing, now including one optional string.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same two existing state serializations per attempted context update, each enlarged by at most one scalar field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same whole-state serialization occurred without billableOwnerKey.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous local work on entitlement updates, not rendering/input/scroll paths; unchanged responses return before storage and events.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed-size entitlement state for one account; owner key length controls only a small linear increase in two JSON serializations and stored bytes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entitlement resolution is cancellation-controlled by pendingResolveCts, and context updates are sequential synchronous mutations around a barrier. No new parallel work is spawned by parsing or context-key binding.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Exact repeated responses compare equal and return before storage writes and context-key events. The cached profile state is replaced only on actual state changes; no map or history retains past owner values.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: state comparison, persistence, and event propagation were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Server key length is not explicitly bounded here, but it is a single account identifier already present in the bounded entitlement response; there is no repeated collection or retained history.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no repeated expensive operation, unbounded retention, or hot UI-path work is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and traced entitlement parsing/state persistence through assignment-filter events to filesystem, serialization, request-service, and TAS network boundaries. The change adds bounded scalar work and one intentional, coalesced assignment refresh only when the effective billable owner changes; no actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
